titel: The Book of Sentences: four Beguins handed to the secular arm (Toulouse, 1322)
autor: Bernard Gui (c. 1261–1331), Dominican, inquisitor of Toulouse 1307–1323, with the vicars of the bishops of the province, in the Liber sententiarum inquisitionis Tholosanae written by the inquisition's notaries
quelle: Liber sententiarum inquisitionis Tholosanae ab anno Christi 1307 ad annum 1323, printed from the original manuscript by Philipp van Limborch, Historia inquisitionis (Amsterdam: Henricus Wetstenius, 1692), second part, pp. 334 and 381–393 (manuscript fols. 196–203 b). Internet Archive, per_witchcraft-in-europe-and-america_historia-inquisitionis_limborch-philippus_1692_2_578. Public domain.
hinweis: Limborch printed the book of sentences from the original register of the inquisition of Toulouse, then in private hands, now London, British Library, Add. MS 4697. His Latin is carried as he printed it, transcribed from the page images because the machine reading of the long s is unusable: the medieval spelling (conbustus, dyocesis, sentencia) and the ampersand are kept, the long s is set as s, and the manuscript folio numbers printed in his margin are given with each page. The excerpts follow the four persons sentenced to the secular arm in the last general sermon of Bernard Gui's register; cuts are marked […], and what is cut is summarized in the notes. The English is this site's working translation (CC0). These are the words of the court, not of the accused: the Beguins' beliefs reach us as articles drawn up by their judges from their confessions.

sections.titel: The general sermon of Toulouse (12 September 1322)
sections.blurb: Bernard Gui, inquisitor, with the vicars of eight bishops, before the king's court, the consuls and 'a great multitude of clergy and people' in the church of Saint-Étienne.

units.orig:
ACTA SERMONIS FACTI THOLOSE ANNO DOMINI Mº. CCCº. XXIIº.
IN nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi amen. Anno ejusdem Domini benedicti Mº. CCCº. XXIIº. dominica infra octabas nativitatis beate Marie Virginis, qua intitulatur pridie ydus septembris Tholose ad honorem omnipotentis Dei & sancte Romane ecclesie, cui presidet sanctissimus pater ac dominus Johannes papa XXIIus fuerunt facte gracie & injuncte penitencie & late diffinitive sentencie & acta alia que secuntur in sermone publico more inquisitorum facto Tholose in ecclesia sancti Stephani. In quibus convenerunt & concordaverunt religiosus vir frater Bernardus Guidonis ordinis predicatorum inquisitor heretice pravitatis in regno Francie per sedem apostolicam deputatus pro se, […] presente ibidem curia regali & consulibus seu capitulariis Tholosanis, & cleri ac populi multitudine copiosa.
units.en:
Acts of the sermon held at Toulouse in the year of the Lord 1322.
In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen. In the year of the same blessed Lord 1322, on the Sunday within the octave of the Nativity of the blessed Virgin Mary, which is called the day before the Ides of September, at Toulouse, to the honour of almighty God and of the holy Roman Church, over which our most holy father and lord Pope John XXII presides, the graces granted, the penances imposed, the definitive sentences pronounced and the other acts that follow were done in a public sermon, in the manner of the inquisitors, held at Toulouse in the church of Saint-Étienne. In which the religious man brother Bernard Gui of the order of Preachers, inquisitor of heretical depravity in the kingdom of France deputed by the apostolic see, agreed and concurred, for himself, […] in the presence of the royal court and the consuls or capitouls of Toulouse, and of a great multitude of clergy and people.
units.note: 12 September 1322. A 'general sermon' (sermo generalis) was the public ceremony in which the inquisitor read out penances and sentences before the authorities and the people: at this one, according to the Liber's own index, the fourteenth recorded in the book. The cut names the vicars and commissaries of the bishops of Montauban, Albi, Rodez, Mirepoix, Rieux, Saint-Papoul and the archbishop of Toulouse who sat with Gui; among them a Franciscan, brother Roger de Aset. The sentences carried below were read at the end of this sermon.

sections.blurb: A Beguin who had abjured, sworn to betray the others, drank wine with two fugitives, told them how the Beguins burned at Narbonne had died 'bravely and strongly', and then had them arrested.

units.orig: […] quantum ad nos pertinet de duabus personis infrascriptis per inquisicionem factam invenimus, nec non per confessionem propriam factam in judicio anno Domini Mº. CCCº. XXIIº. in vigilia apostolorum Petri & Pauli, Guilielmi Ruffi de cincta gavella, filii quondam Petri Ruffi, beguini dyocesis Mirapiscensis, qui se dicit esse de tercio ordine seu de tercia regula sancti Francisci, quam asserit se fuisse professum cum publico instrumento, quod ipse postquam abjuraverat omnem heresim & errorem cujuscunque secte, & specialiter & expresse errores & opiniones erroneas quos & quas crediderat, qui errores & que opiniones inveniuntur teneri & credi à quibusdam qui dicunt se esse fratres de tercia regula sancti Francisci, & beguini vulgariter apellantur, sub pena que de jure debetur relapsis in heresim in judicio abjuratam, promiseratque atque juraverat revelare & detegere prelatis & inquisitoribus omnes & singulos quoscunque sciret aut crederet tenere predictos errores beguinorum, aut aliquos ex eisdem. Ex tunc audivit & scivit per quandam personam, quam in confessione sua nominat, esse in domo dicte persone apud cinctam gavellam Petrum arruffati de Narbona, & Petrum tort de monte regali, quos ipse antea noverat & sciebat esse de affectione & credencia beguinorum quo ad errores seu opiniones erroneas ipsorum, quorum primus fuit postmodum judicatus hereticus & conbustus, secundus vero per sentenciam inmuratus, & venit ad eos ad dictam domum, & osculatus fuit & bene recollegit eos, & tunc fuit in dubio si eos faceret capi vel non […].
units.en: […] As far as it concerns us, we have found by the inquiry made, and also by the confession made in court in the year of the Lord 1322 on the vigil of the apostles Peter and Paul, concerning the two persons written below: that Guillaume Ruffi of Ceintegabelle, son of the late Pierre Ruffi, a Beguin of the diocese of Mirepoix, who says he is of the third order or third rule of Saint Francis, which he asserts he professed by public instrument, after he had abjured every heresy and error of any sect, and specially and expressly the errors and erroneous opinions he had believed, which are found to be held and believed by certain people who say they are brothers of the third rule of Saint Francis and are commonly called Beguins, under the penalty due by law to those who relapse into a heresy abjured in court, and had promised and sworn to reveal and disclose to the prelates and inquisitors each and every person he knew or believed to hold those errors of the Beguins, or any of them: after that he heard and learned from a certain person, whom he names in his confession, that Pierre Arrufat of Narbonne and Pierre Tort of Montréal were in that person's house at Ceintegabelle, whom he had known before and knew to be of the affection and belief of the Beguins as to their errors or erroneous opinions; the first of whom was afterwards judged a heretic and burned, the second by sentence walled up; and he came to them at that house, kissed them and received them warmly, and was then in doubt whether to have them arrested or not […].
units.note: 28 June 1322. The 'third order' was the Franciscan order of penitents for lay people; the Beguins of Languedoc were its members or claimed to be, followers of the Spiritual Franciscans and of Peter John Olivi. 'Walled up' (inmuratus): sentenced to the inquisition's prison, the murus. Pierre Arrufat, 'afterwards judged a heretic and burned', is one of the burned the Liber names without carrying his sentence.

units.titel: 'Nothing was left for him but the fire'
units.orig: […] petivit etiam ab eis & audivit quare venerant ad dictam villam, videlicet quia audiverant quod beguini illarum parcium fuerant capti per inquisitorem & habuerant tribulaciones, & venerant ad sciendum qualiter erat eis, & petiverunt qualiter transiverat ipse cum inquisitore, & ipse respondit eis quod fecerat voluntatem ejus, & opportebat quod de cetero staret in quiete, quia aliter non restabat ei nisi ignis. Ipse etiam petivit ab eis qualiter se habuerant illi beguini qui hoc anno dominica prima in quadragesima Narbone fuerant condempnati & conbusti, & ipsi responderunt ei quod valenter & fortiter se habuerant. Item ipse misit pro vino & bibit cum eis in dicta domo, & dixit eis ad partem quod quando recessisset ab eis exirent & recederent de dicta domo, ita quod quando ipse reverteretur ad dictam domum non inveniret eos ibi, & cum recessisset ab eis & etiam ante aliquantulum inceperat cogitare quod periculum posset sibi inminere nisi faceret eos capi propter juramentum quod fecerat de capiendis hereticis & maxime beguinis, & tunc ivit ad unum de consulibus ville, & cum eo procuravit quod predicti duo beguini caperentur, & fuerunt capti eodem sero extra villam de qua jam exiverant recedentes. […]
units.en: […] He also asked them, and heard, why they had come to that town: namely because they had heard that the Beguins of those parts had been arrested by the inquisitor and had suffered tribulations, and they had come to learn how it went with them; and they asked how it had gone for him with the inquisitor, and he answered them that he had done his will, and that from now on he had to keep quiet, because otherwise nothing was left for him but the fire. He also asked them how those Beguins had borne themselves who this year, on the first Sunday of Lent, had been condemned and burned at Narbonne; and they answered him that they had borne themselves bravely and strongly. Item, he sent for wine and drank with them in that house, and told them aside that when he had left them they should go out and leave the house, so that when he came back he would not find them there. And when he had left them, and even a little before, he had begun to think that he might be in danger unless he had them arrested, because of the oath he had taken to arrest heretics and above all Beguins; and then he went to one of the consuls of the town and arranged with him that the two Beguins be arrested; and they were arrested the same evening outside the town, which they had already left. […]
units.note: The Beguins burned at Narbonne on the first Sunday of Lent 'this year', early in 1322, are not named. The rest of the case against Ruffi, cut here, concerns his intimacy with a married woman, whom he taught that lying naked together without consummating was a merit 'for the love of God', a teaching he said he had from another Beguin; it was she who accused him in court. The inquisitor used it to show him 'falsely converted and perjured'.

sections.blurb: A Beguin who took off his penitential crosses: the pope cannot allow the friars granaries, the four burned at Marseille are martyrs, John XXII is a heretic, Olivi is in paradise and Rome is Babylon; a litany with the names of about seventy condemned, read aloud before the inquisitor; and the sentence handing him and Ruffi to the secular arm.

units.titel: Pierre Dominici of Narbonne, who took off his crosses
units.orig: ¶ Item per confessionem factam in judicio legitime nobis constat, quod Petrus Dominici alias cognominatus de honors filius quondam Raymundi Dominici oriundus de Narbona beguinus de tercia regula sancti Francisci quam asserit se fuisse professum, & portat habitum cum mantello, captus & deprehensus apud caniacum Rivensis dyocesis cum Petro hospitali & cum Petro Guiraudi, olim captus fuit in Narbona & detentus in carcere domini archiepiscopi Narbonensis, cum quibusdam aliis beguinis, fuitque confessus in judicio coram officiali prefati domini archiepiscopi articulos quos credebat, propter quos fuit postmodum in sermone publico facto Narbone per prefatum archiepiscopum & inquisitorem Carcassonensem heretice pravitatis penitenciatus & punitus ut portaret cruces de filtro vestibus suis pro illis que confessus fuerat se credidisse & tenuisse de opinionibus erroneis beguinorum, dictamque penitenciam suscepit, & articulos quos confessus fuerat revocavit, & omnem errorem & heresim in judicio abjuravit. Postmodum vero dictas cruces nomine penitencie sibi inpositas temeritate propria deposuit per seipsum credens se Deum offendisse eas recipiendo & offendere in portando.
units.en: ¶ Item, by the confession made in court it is lawfully established for us that Pierre Dominici, also called 'de Honors', son of the late Raymond Dominici, a native of Narbonne, a Beguin of the third rule of Saint Francis, which he asserts he professed, who wears the habit with the mantle, arrested and taken at Caniacum in the diocese of Rieux together with Pierre Hospitalis and Pierre Guiraud, was formerly arrested at Narbonne and held in the prison of the lord archbishop of Narbonne with some other Beguins, and confessed in court before the archbishop's official the articles he believed, for which he was afterwards, in a public sermon held at Narbonne by the archbishop and the inquisitor of Carcassonne, given penance and punished by having to wear crosses of felt on his clothes for what he had confessed to have believed and held of the erroneous opinions of the Beguins; and he accepted that penance, revoked the articles he had confessed, and abjured every error and heresy in court. But afterwards, on his own rash authority, he took off the crosses imposed on him as penance, believing that he had offended God by accepting them and offended him by wearing them.
units.note: The crosses were two yellow felt crosses, front and back, 'two and a half palms long and two wide', which penitents had to wear on their outer clothes for life (the form is spelled out in the Liber's penances, for example Pierre de Fonte's at Pamiers, p. 206). Taking them off was relapse. Caniacum in the diocese of Rieux is Cagnac or a place of similar name; the Liber spells the place of arrest 'cariacum' in Pierre Hospitalis' case.

units.orig: ¶ Predictus Petrus Dominici postquam confessus fuerat in judicio de hiis que prius conmiserat in erroribus beguinorum, […] ex tunc abjecta dicta penitencia contra proprium juramentum deprehensus fuit in fuga latitans cum predictis duobus Petro hospitalis & Petro Guiraudi sectatoribus ejusdem dogmatis & erroris. Et examinatus confessus est in judicio se credere & tenere esse vera illa que prius confessus fuerat & abjuraverat, & penitet se ea abjurasse. Item credit & asserit quod dominus papa non potest concedere fratribus minoribus quod habeant cellaria seu granaria ad conservandum bladum vel vinum. Item quod non potest nec potuit facere aut fecisse constitucionem seu declaracionem, & quod tali declaracioni facte per eum non est obediendum, quia est contra votum fratrum minorum. Item quod non potest concedere secundum Deum fratribus minoribus quod portent habitus magnos latos seu tinctos. Item quod non potest facere de plenitudine potestatis quod frater minor fiat frater alterius religionis vel ordinis ubi habeat possessiones vel aliquid in conmuni, nec frater minor debet obedire pape in hoc, & si papa in hoc dispensaret peccaret. Item quod papa non potest facere quod frater minor factus episcopus sit dominus rerum temporalium spectancium ad episcopatum, nec potest quod pecuniam manu sua contractet, set faciat dispensari & ministrari bona mobilia per alium pauperibus. Item credit & asserit quod euangelium Christi est regula sancti Francisci in castitate & paupertate & obediencia, & in istis tribus seu in aliquo istorum trium papa non potest dispensare, & si dispensaret tunc faceret contra vitam Christi & contra euangelium. […]
units.en: ¶ The said Pierre Dominici, after he had confessed in court what he had previously committed in the errors of the Beguins, […] then, having thrown off the penance against his own oath, was taken hiding in flight with the said two, Pierre Hospitalis and Pierre Guiraud, followers of the same doctrine and error. And examined, he confessed in court that he believes and holds to be true what he had confessed and abjured before, and regrets having abjured it. Item, he believes and asserts that the lord pope cannot grant the Friars Minor that they have cellars or granaries to keep grain or wine. Item, that he cannot, and could not, make such a constitution or declaration, and that such a declaration made by him is not to be obeyed, because it is against the vow of the Friars Minor. Item, that he cannot, according to God, grant the Friars Minor that they wear large, wide or dyed habits. Item, that he cannot by the fullness of his power make a Friar Minor become a brother of another religion or order in which he would have possessions or anything in common; nor must a Friar Minor obey the pope in this, and if the pope dispensed in this he would sin. Item, that the pope cannot make a Friar Minor who has become a bishop lord of the temporal things belonging to the bishopric, nor let him handle money with his own hand; he must have the movable goods dispensed and administered to the poor by another. Item, he believes and asserts that the Gospel of Christ is the rule of Saint Francis in chastity, poverty and obedience, and that in these three, or in any one of them, the pope cannot dispense, and if he dispensed he would act against the life of Christ and against the Gospel. […]
units.note: The 'constitution or declaration' on cellars, granaries and habits is John XXII's Quorundam exigit of 1317 (Decr. Exigit [4]), which left both to the superiors' judgement and ordered the Spirituals to put off their short habits. The article on passing to 'another order … where he would have possessions in common' answers the pope's transfer of Spiritual friars to other orders in 1317–18. The cut continues with articles on vows of chastity.

units.titel: The martyrs of Marseille and Narbonne; John XXII a heretic
units.orig: […] Item asserit se credere & tenere quod illi IIIIor fratres minores qui fuerunt apud Massiliam per judicium inquisitoris heretice pravitatis de maturo consilio tanquam heretici condempnati à IIIIor annis citra, & etiam beguini seu fratres de tercio ordine penitencium seu de tercia regula sancti Francisci qui fuerunt condempnati tanquam heretici per judicium prelatorum & inquisitoris Carcassonensis heretice pravitatis à tribus à duobus & ab uno annis citra in provincia Narbonensi in diversis locis seu villis fuerunt & erant catholici tempore condempnacionis sue, & sunt facti martires, & fuerunt passi pro veritate euangelica sustinenda. Item quod omnes illi qui condempnaverunt eos, videlicet prelati & inquisitores, & etiam omnes qui consenserunt in condempnacione predictorum, & etiam dominus papa si consentiit in hoc, erraverunt & facti sunt heretici, & nisi penituerint dampnabuntur. Item quod dominus papa Johannes XXIIus est malus & hereticus, & est extra ecclesiam Dei propter hoc quia persecutus est pauperes beguinos de tercia regula sancti Francisci. Item quod amisit totaliter potestatem jurisdictionis sue ligandi & solvendi, nec ipse reputat eum esse papam, nec se esse eidem subditum, quia condempnat vel consentit quod beguini tanquam heretici condempnentur. […]
units.en: […] Item, he asserts that he believes and holds that those four Friars Minor who were condemned as heretics at Marseille by the judgement of the inquisitor of heretical depravity, after mature counsel, four years ago, and also the Beguins or brothers of the third order of penitents or third rule of Saint Francis who were condemned as heretics by the judgement of the prelates and of the inquisitor of heretical depravity of Carcassonne three, two and one years ago in the province of Narbonne, in various places or towns, were and are catholics at the time of their condemnation, and have become martyrs, and suffered for upholding the truth of the Gospel. Item, that all those who condemned them, namely the prelates and inquisitors, and also all who consented to their condemnation, and also the lord pope if he consented to it, erred and became heretics, and will be damned unless they repent. Item, that the lord Pope John XXII is wicked and a heretic, and is outside the Church of God, because he has persecuted the poor Beguins of the third rule of Saint Francis. Item, that he has wholly lost his power of jurisdiction, of binding and loosing, and he does not hold him to be pope, nor himself to be his subject, because he condemns, or consents that the Beguins be condemned as heretics. […]
units.note: The four Friars Minor burned at Marseille in May 1318 were Spirituals who refused to obey Quorundam exigit (Decr. Exigit [5]). 'Three, two and one years ago': the burnings of Beguins at Narbonne, Béziers, Lunel and elsewhere in 1319–1321. This is the reasoning the game's burned make: obedience to the pope, who made the granaries lawful, was obedience to a heretic.

units.titel: Olivi in paradise; Rome the great whore
units.orig: […] Item asserit se credere & tenere quod tota doctrina & scriptura fratris Petri Johannis Olivi de ordine fratrum minorum est vera & catholica secundum intellectum quem habuit in ea sicut credit esse fidelem & catholicam doctrinam sancti Johannis euangeliste secundum intellectum quem habuit in eadem, & addidit se credere quod sicut Johannes euangelista est in paradiso, ita credit fratrem Petrum Johannis predictum esse in paradiso, quamvis sanctus Johannes habeat majorem gloriam. Item asserit quod si papa condempnaret doctrinam seu scripturam prefati Petri Johannis, ipse non reputaret eam condempnatam quantumcunque poneret dictam condempnacionem sub mille bullis, & quantumcunque condempnaret eam de consilio cardinalium & omnium prelatorum, vel etiam tocius concilii generalis. […] Item asserit se credere & tenere esse vera illa que frater Petrus Johannis scripsit in postilla super apocalipsim de babilone meretrice magna sedente super bestiam, per quam intelligit & exponit esse ecclesiam Romanam quam dicit esse babilonem meretricem magnam & carnalem ecclesiam. Item eandem ecclesiam Romanam sub nomine babilonis dicit esse dampnandam & reiciendam & exterminandam à Christo in isto sexto statu ecclesie quem dicit nunc esse, & dicit ecclesiam spiritualem esse incipiendam & reformandam rejecta ecclesia carnali, sicut vetus synagoga Judeorum fuit rejecta à Christo incipiente euangelio Christi & statu ecclesie primitive.
units.en: […] Item, he asserts that he believes and holds that the whole teaching and writing of brother Peter John Olivi of the order of Friars Minor is true and catholic, in the sense he gave it, just as he believes the teaching of Saint John the Evangelist faithful and catholic in the sense he gave it; and he added that he believes that, as John the Evangelist is in paradise, so brother Peter John is in paradise, though Saint John has the greater glory. Item, he asserts that if the pope condemned the teaching or writing of Peter John, he would not hold it condemned, however much he put the condemnation under a thousand bulls, and however much he condemned it on the advice of the cardinals and all the prelates, or even of a whole general council. […] Item, he asserts that he believes and holds to be true what brother Peter John wrote in his commentary on the Apocalypse about Babylon, the great whore sitting on the beast, by which he understands and expounds the Roman Church, which he calls Babylon the great whore and the carnal Church. Item, he says that this same Roman Church, under the name of Babylon, is to be damned, rejected and destroyed by Christ in this sixth state of the Church, which he says is now; and he says that the spiritual Church is to begin and be reformed once the carnal Church is rejected, as the old synagogue of the Jews was rejected by Christ when the Gospel of Christ and the state of the primitive Church began.
units.note: Peter John Olivi (d. 1298), the Franciscan theologian of Narbonne whose tomb the Beguins venerated, taught that 'poor use' belonged to the Franciscan vow (Exivi [4]) and read the Apocalypse as a history of the Church in seven states, the sixth beginning with Francis. His commentary was condemned by John XXII in 1326; the sentence below already cites an examination of it by eight masters of theology. The phrase about the synagogue is the sentence's report of Olivi's typology, printed as it stands.

units.orig: ¶ Prefatus frater P. Dominici perseverans in predictis erroribus & in fuga captus & deprehensus in judicio sepius requisitus quod predictos errores omnes & singulos revocaret per duos menses & amplius obstinatus in eis revocare penitus recusavit. Tandem vero IIIº. Kalendas Junii constitutus in judicio recognovit se predictos errores omnes & singulos tenuisse & credidisse, & tunc dixit se velle penitere & abjurare & revocare errores & opiniones erroneas in predictis, unde in judicio constitutus coram inquisitore Tholosano abjuravit omnem errorem & omnem heresim […]. ¶ Postmodum vero prefatus Petrus Dominici confingens se alienatum à sensu predictam sectam & heresim ejusdemque secte devios sectatores laudans illos quos prius condempnatos per ecclesie judicium tanquam hereticos audiverat & sciebat eorumque nomina memoriter retinebat ausus est conscribere in letania quam manu propria scripsit inter sanctos martires & virgines ac confessores more ecclesiastico, letaniam dicendo nunc alte nunc demisse, dampnatorum hominum oraciones & suffragia pluribus vicibus & multo tempore inplorando ex devocione quam ad ipsos conceperat & habebat, & credebat eorum oraciones sibi valere apud Deum sicut in judicio constitutus asseruit medio juramento, & letaniam ipsam in qua prefatorum dampnatorum hominum nomina manu sua conscripserat numero circiter septuaginta coram inquisitore perlegit perlectamque ab eodem inquisitore habuit & recepit, quod non est dubium prefatum Petrum Dominici ex approbati à se prius consequencia id fecisse.
units.en: ¶ The said brother Pierre Dominici, persisting in these errors and taken in flight, was often required in court for two months and more to revoke each and all of these errors, and obstinately refused altogether to revoke them. At last, on the third day before the Kalends of June, standing in court, he acknowledged that he had held and believed each and all of these errors, and then said he wished to repent, abjure and revoke the errors and erroneous opinions in them; and so, standing in court before the inquisitor of Toulouse, he abjured every error and every heresy […]. ¶ But afterwards the said Pierre Dominici, pretending to be out of his mind, and praising that sect and heresy and the misguided followers of that sect, those whom he had heard and knew to have been condemned as heretics by the judgement of the Church, and whose names he kept in his memory, dared to write them into a litany, which he wrote with his own hand, among the holy martyrs, virgins and confessors, in the manner of the Church; and saying the litany, now aloud, now softly, he implored the prayers and intercession of the condemned many times and for a long while, out of the devotion he had conceived and had for them, and believed that their prayers availed him before God, as he asserted in court on oath; and the litany itself, in which he had written with his own hand the names of those condemned, about seventy in number, he read through before the inquisitor, and the inquisitor had it read through and took it; so that there is no doubt that Pierre Dominici did this as a consequence of what he had approved before.
units.note: 30 May 1322. The litany is the Beguins' own list of their dead: about seventy names, read aloud before Bernard Gui, who took it. The Liber does not copy the names. The game's list of the burned can therefore name only those whose names the documents keep; the seventy stand behind them, uncounted.

units.titel: Like a dog to its vomit: the sentence
units.orig: ¶ Et quoniam prefatus Guilielmus Ruffi & Petrus Dominici predictus postquam alias confessi fuerant se commisisse in crimine heresis & in erroribus & opinionibus erroneis beguinorum predictorum, promiserantque atque juraverant parere mandatis ecclesie & inquisitorum & abjuraverant omnem heresim in judicio, fuerantque absoluti à sentencia exconmunicacionis lata à canone contra tales, ex tunc tanquam canis ad vomitum redeuntes culpis veteribus novas addere non verendo deprehensi sunt iterum sicut supra premittitur conmisisse, prefatus Petrus Dominici in abjuratos errores relabendo, & prefatus Guilielmus Ruffi favorem inexcusabilem inpendendo & dogmatisacionem erroneam prefate mulieri faciendo, per hoc se falso & ficte conversos & inpenitentes ac perjuros & de tam enormi crimine se incorrigibiles ostendendo, omnique gracia & audiencia tanquam relapsi in heresim fecerint se indignos, ita quod promissionibus & juramentis suis nulla sit fides de cetero adhibenda. Idcirco nos prefati inquisitor & vicarii ac conmissarii […] dicimus & per diffinitivam sentenciam in hiis scriptis pronunciamus & declaramus ipsos esse relapsos in heresim à se in judicio abjuratam, & cum ecclesia ulterius non habeat quid faciat pro suis demeritis contra ipsos, Idcirco eosdem tanquam relapsos relinquimus brachio & judicio curie secularis, affectuose rogantes prout suadent canonice sancciones venerabilem & discretum virum dominum Johannem Marchi judicem majorem domini nostri regis & locum tenentem domini senescalli Tholose ac tenentes locum vicarii Tholosani & alios judices & curiales domini regis hic presentes quatinus citra mortem & membrorum mutilacionem circa ipsos suam sentenciam ac judicium moderentur. Volumus autem & mandamus quatinus prefatis Guilielmo Ruffi & Petro Dominici, si digne pecierint & vere penituerint, sacramentum penitencie & eucharistie concedantur. Lata fuit hec sentencia in presenti sermone, anno die & loco presentibus testibus & notariis quibus supra.
units.en: ¶ And since the said Guillaume Ruffi and the said Pierre Dominici, after they had formerly confessed that they had offended in the crime of heresy and in the errors and erroneous opinions of the said Beguins, and had promised and sworn to obey the commands of the Church and of the inquisitors, and had abjured every heresy in court, and had been absolved from the sentence of excommunication pronounced by the canon against such people, then, returning like a dog to its vomit and not fearing to add new faults to old ones, have been found to have offended again, as set out above, Pierre Dominici by relapsing into the errors he had abjured, and Guillaume Ruffi by giving inexcusable favour and teaching error to the said woman, and have thereby shown themselves falsely and feignedly converted, impenitent and perjured and incorrigible in so enormous a crime, and have made themselves unworthy, as relapsed into heresy, of all grace and hearing, so that no faith is to be given henceforth to their promises and oaths: therefore we, the said inquisitor, vicars and commissaries […] say, and by definitive sentence in these writings pronounce and declare, that they have relapsed into the heresy they abjured in court; and since the Church has nothing further it can do against them for their deserts, therefore we leave them, as relapsed, to the arm and judgement of the secular court, affectionately asking, as the canonical sanctions advise, the venerable and discreet man lord Jean Marchi, chief judge of our lord the king and lieutenant of the lord seneschal of Toulouse, and those who hold the place of the vicar of Toulouse, and the other judges and officers of the lord king present here, to moderate their sentence and judgement concerning them short of death and the mutilation of limbs. We will and command, however, that the sacraments of penance and the Eucharist be granted to Guillaume Ruffi and Pierre Dominici if they ask worthily and truly repent. This sentence was pronounced in the present sermon, in the year, on the day and at the place, and before the witnesses and notaries, named above.
units.note: 'Like a dog to its vomit': Proverbs 26:11 and 2 Peter 2:22. To 'leave to the secular arm' (relinquere curiae saeculari) was the inquisitor's form for handing over to execution; the plea to spare life and limb was prescribed by canon law and was a formality. For relapsed heretics the secular penalty was burning. The Liber records the relaxation, not the execution. Note the last sentence: the relapsed who repented received the sacraments before the fire.

sections.blurb: The pope who allowed granaries has ceased to be pope; whoever says Christ had anything, of his own or in common, is a heretic; a Beguin who would not swear to name his companions; and the sentence of 'obstinate heretics' who 'choose rather to die for their errors than be converted'.

units.titel: Pierre Hospitalis, called Christiani, of Montpellier
units.orig: IN nomine Domini amen. Quoniam nos frater Bernardus Guidonis ordinis predicatorum inquisitor heretice pravitatis in regno Francie per sedem apostolicam deputatus, & Raymundus bernardi de sancta Arthemia canonicus Rivensis vicarius generalis, & Guilielmus Rocherii archipresbiter & officialis Rivensis conmissarius in hac parte reverendi in Christo patris domini B. Dei gracia Rivensis episcopi, invenimus per inquisicionem que facta est & fit generaliter contra omnes infectos aut suspectos aut notatos de heretica pravitate, nec non contra errores ac opiniones erroneas tam scismaticas quam hereticas quorundam qui se dicunt fratres de ordine penitencium apellato, & profitentur ut asserunt terciam regulam sancti Francisci cum publico instrumento, & portant distinctum habitum, & in provincia Narbonensi & Tholosana beguini vulgariter apellantur, extollentes se adversus sanctam Romanam ecclesiam & apostolicam sedem, & contra potestatem ac primatum domini nostri pape, & contra potestatem clavium ecclesie, ac etiam contra sanam doctrinam scripture sacre, quam Romana servat & docet ecclesia. Nec non per confessionem & assercionem factam in judicio legitime nobis constat, quod Petrus hospitalis qui alias faciebat se cognominari Christiani, filius quondam Raymundi hospitalis, oriundus de monte pessullano, captus & deprehensus apud cariacum Rivensis dyocesis, olim alias captus fuit pro facto beguinorum in Narbona & detentus in carcere domini archiepiscopi Narbonensis, […] fueruntque sibi inposite & injuncte per ipsos cruces de filtro crocei coloris ad portandum in vestibus suis, & alique peregrinaciones in penitenciam […]. Postmodum vero penituit & doluit, quia revocaverat illa que confessus fuerat se credere & tenere, & quia dictas cruces nomine penitencie susceperat, easque deposuit temeritate propria per se ipsum, dicens se credere quod quanto plus eas portaret tanto amplius hoc esset in Dei vituperium & offensam, & quod illi qui eas sibi inposuerunt inponendo & ipse qui eas suscepit in suscipiendo & portando Deum graviter offenderunt.
units.en: In the name of the Lord, amen. Since we, brother Bernard Gui of the order of Preachers, inquisitor of heretical depravity in the kingdom of France deputed by the apostolic see, and Raymond Bernard of Sainte-Arthémie, canon of Rieux, vicar general, and Guillaume Rocher, archpriest and official of Rieux, commissary in this matter of the reverend father in Christ lord B., by the grace of God bishop of Rieux, have found by the inquiry which has been and is being made generally against all who are infected with, suspected of or noted for heretical depravity, and also against the errors and erroneous opinions, both schismatic and heretical, of certain people who call themselves brothers of the order called of penitents, and profess, as they assert, the third rule of Saint Francis by public instrument, and wear a distinct habit, and in the provinces of Narbonne and Toulouse are commonly called Beguins, raising themselves against the holy Roman Church and the apostolic see, against the power and primacy of our lord the pope, against the power of the keys of the Church, and also against the sound doctrine of holy scripture which the Roman Church keeps and teaches: and by the confession and assertion made in court it is lawfully established for us that Pierre Hospitalis, who at other times had himself called Christiani, son of the late Raymond Hospitalis, a native of Montpellier, arrested and taken at Cariacum in the diocese of Rieux, was formerly arrested at Narbonne in the matter of the Beguins and held in the prison of the lord archbishop of Narbonne, […] and crosses of yellow felt were imposed and enjoined on him by them to wear on his clothes, and some pilgrimages as penance […]. But afterwards he repented and grieved that he had revoked what he had confessed to believe and hold, and that he had accepted the crosses as penance; and he took them off on his own rash authority, saying that he believed that the more he wore them the more it would be to God's dishonour and offence, and that those who imposed them on him, in imposing them, and he who accepted them, in accepting and wearing them, had gravely offended God.
units.note: 'Christiani': the Beguins sometimes took new names. The cut gives his confession and abjuration at Narbonne before the archbishop's vicars and the inquisitor of Carcassonne, Jean de Beaune.

units.titel: The pope who allowed granaries has lost his power
units.orig: ¶ Predictus Petrus hospitalis postquam confessus fuerat in judicio, […] ex tunc deprehensus est in fuga cum quibusdam aliis conplicibus & sectatoribus ejusdem dogmatis & erroris. Et examinatus in judicio confessus est se credere & tenere quod illa constitucio decretalis seu declaracio quam dominus Johannes papa XXIIus fecit super regula sancti Francisci per quam concedit fratribus minoribus quod ad arbitrium prelatorum dicti ordinis possint congregare bladum & vinum pro vite fratrum necessariis, & reponere & conservare in granariis vel cellariis in conmuni ad suum usum, falsa est & iniqua & in destructionem euangelice paupertatis, & idem papa erravit in hoc & facit errare fratres minores, & si hoc ipsum pertinaciter & obstinate sustineat ex hoc ipso hereticus est effectus, & ipse Petrus hospitalis eumdem papam reputat esse hereticum. Item omnes illos qui scienter consenserunt in dicta constitucione seu declaracione & in hoc pertinaciter perseverant ipse reputat & credit esse hereticos, sive sint cardinales sive prelati alii sive etiam fratres minores. Item quod idem dominus papa ex eo quia factus est hereticus dictam constitucionem faciendo papalem perdidit potestatem, hoc tamen adjecto, si de jure est vel sit quod papa factus hereticus papalem perdat potestatem ipso jure. […] Item credidit & adhuc credit Romanam ecclesiam nunc non habere papam, set credit vacare papatum, quia licet dominus Johannes papa XXIIus qui nunc est à principio fuerit verus papa, tamen modo non est nec fuit set desiit esse papa ex quo fecit dictam constitucionem, & perseveravit & adhuc perseverat eam pertinaciter sustinendo. Item non credit quod prefatus dominus papa possit facere aliquos prelatos, & si faceret ipse non crederet eos esse prelatos. Item credidit & adhuc credit & reputat esse hereticum omnem hominem qui dicit & credit quod Christus & apostoli habuerint aliquid seu aliquas divicias in proprio vel conmuni. […]
units.en: ¶ The said Pierre Hospitalis, after he had confessed in court, […] was then taken in flight with some other accomplices and followers of the same doctrine and error. And examined in court, he confessed that he believes and holds that the decretal constitution or declaration which the lord Pope John XXII made on the rule of Saint Francis, by which he grants the Friars Minor that, at the discretion of the prelates of that order, they may gather grain and wine for the necessities of the friars' life, and store and keep them in granaries or cellars in common for their use, is false and wicked and for the destruction of evangelical poverty; and that the pope erred in this and makes the Friars Minor err; and that if he maintains this pertinaciously and obstinately he has by that very fact become a heretic; and Pierre Hospitalis holds this pope to be a heretic. Item, all who knowingly consented to that constitution or declaration and persist in it pertinaciously he holds and believes to be heretics, whether cardinals or other prelates or even Friars Minor. Item, that the lord pope, since he became a heretic by making that constitution, lost the papal power; adding, however, 'if it is or be the law that a pope who has become a heretic loses the papal power by law itself'. […] Item, he believed and still believes that the Roman Church now has no pope, but believes the papacy to be vacant, because although the lord Pope John XXII, who now is, was at the beginning a true pope, now he is not and was not, but ceased to be pope from the moment he made that constitution, and persisted and still persists in maintaining it pertinaciously. Item, he does not believe that the said lord pope can make any prelates, and if he did, he would not believe them to be prelates. Item, he believed and still believes, and holds to be a heretic, every man who says and believes that Christ and the apostles had anything, or any riches, of their own or in common. […]
units.note: The constitution is Quorundam exigit (1317), which left granaries and cellars to the superiors' judgement (Decr. Exigit [4]). The last article is the Beguins' form of the Franciscan thesis that John XXII condemned fourteen months later (Decr. Nonnullos [1]): in 1322 it is the Beguin who calls the opposite heresy. The careful proviso 'if it is the law that a heretical pope loses his power' is the canonists' question the Franciscan exiles would press against John XXII from 1328.

units.titel: Pierre Guiraud, who would not swear to betray
units.orig: ¶ Item per confessionem factam in judicio legitime nobis constat, quod Petrus guiraudi filius quondam Johannis guiraudi de ginhaco dyocesis bitterrensis portans habitum ad modum beguini de bruno sive mantello dicens se esse de penitencia servans ritum vivendi beguinorum captus & deprehensus cum Petro hospitalis & Petro Dominici beguinis de tercia regula sancti Francisci fugitivis apud caniacum Rivensis dyocesis in judicio recognovit & confessus fuit quod ipse alias captus fuit pro facto beguinorum tanquam suspectus de erroribus ipsorum cum quibusdam aliis beguinis quos in confessione sua nominat apud lodonam, fuitque detentus in carcere domini episcopi aliquibus septimanis tanquam suspectus de erroribus beguinorum, & de dicto carcere clam exiit & aufugit. ¶ Predictus Petrus guiraudi in judicio requisitus quod juraret plenam & meram dicere veritatem super facto heresis & erroribus beguinorum moderni temporis, & quod suos conplices & credentes errores consimiles detegeret & revelaret noluit jurare simpliciter & absolute sub tali forma, dicens quod non intendebat jurare nec se juramento obligare ad dicendum aliquid quod esset contra suam conscienciam & in dampnum proximi, & exposuit hoc esse si suos conplices & socios aut conparticipes coram inquisitoribus revelaret. Item asserit se credere & tenere pertinaciter quod dominus papa non potest mutare vel cassare regulam sancti Francisci nec ordinem fratrum minorum, nec tercium ordinem sancti Francisci tollere de medio ordinum aliorum. Item non potest facere quod aliqui fratres minores sint de aliquo alio ordine ubi habeant aliquas divicias in conmuni, quin semper remaneant obligati ad servandum votum paupertatis secundum regulam sancti Francisci, videlicet quod nichil habeant in proprio vel conmuni. Item quod dominus papa Johannes XXIIus fecit injuste quando tradidit in potestatem prelatorum ordinis fratrum minorum illos fratres minores qui tenebant tunc conventum Narbone & bitterris, qui dicebant se velle servare paupertatem & puritatem regule sancti Francisci, de quibus fratribus dicit quod quatuor fuerunt postmodum apud Massiliam à IIIIor annis citra condempnati tanquam heretici per judicium inquisitoris heretice pravitatis. Item asserit se credere fuisse & esse fideles & catholicos & sustinuisse martirium pro veritate regule sancti Francisci predictos IIIIor fratres minores, non obstante judicio quo fuerunt tanquam heretici condempnati. Item credit & asserit esse justos & catholicos & sanctos martires illos beguinos de tercio ordine seu de tercia regula sancti Francisci, qui à tribus & à duobus & ab uno annis citra fuerunt condempnati tanquam heretici per judicium prelatorum & inquisitoris heretice pravitatis in diversis villis seu locis in provincia Narbonensi, quorum aliquos ipse novit & vidit, & fuit cum eis aliquociens conversatus, quos in confessione sua nominat. […]
units.en: ¶ Item, by the confession made in court it is lawfully established for us that Pierre Guiraud, son of the late Jean Guiraud of Ginhac in the diocese of Béziers, who wears a habit in the manner of a Beguin, of brown cloth, or a mantle, saying he is of the penitents and keeping the Beguins' way of life, arrested and taken with Pierre Hospitalis and Pierre Dominici, fugitive Beguins of the third rule of Saint Francis, at Caniacum in the diocese of Rieux, acknowledged and confessed in court that he had formerly been arrested at Lodève in the matter of the Beguins, as suspect of their errors, with some other Beguins whom he names in his confession, and was held some weeks in the lord bishop's prison as suspect of the Beguins' errors, and left the prison secretly and fled. ¶ The said Pierre Guiraud, required in court to swear to tell the full and pure truth on the matter of heresy and of the errors of the Beguins of the present time, and to disclose and reveal his accomplices and those who believed similar errors, would not swear simply and absolutely in that form, saying that he did not intend to swear or bind himself by oath to say anything against his conscience and to his neighbour's harm, and he explained that this would be the case if he revealed his accomplices and companions or fellows before the inquisitors. Item, he asserts that he believes and holds pertinaciously that the lord pope cannot change or annul the rule of Saint Francis or the order of Friars Minor, nor remove the third order of Saint Francis from among the other orders. Item, he cannot make any Friars Minor be of any other order where they would have any riches in common without their remaining always bound to keep the vow of poverty according to the rule of Saint Francis, namely that they have nothing of their own or in common. Item, that the lord Pope John XXII acted unjustly when he handed over to the power of the prelates of the order of Friars Minor those Friars Minor who then held the convents of Narbonne and Béziers and who said they wished to keep the poverty and purity of the rule of Saint Francis; of which friars he says that four were afterwards condemned as heretics at Marseille, four years ago, by the judgement of the inquisitor of heretical depravity. Item, he asserts that he believes that those four Friars Minor were and are faithful and catholic and suffered martyrdom for the truth of the rule of Saint Francis, notwithstanding the judgement by which they were condemned as heretics. Item, he believes and asserts that those Beguins of the third order or third rule of Saint Francis who three, two and one years ago were condemned as heretics by the judgement of the prelates and of the inquisitor of heretical depravity in various towns or places in the province of Narbonne were just and catholic and holy martyrs; some of whom he knew and saw, and was sometimes in their company, and he names them in his confession. […]
units.note: In 1317 the Spiritual friars had taken over the convents of Narbonne and Béziers from the Community; John XXII summoned them to Avignon and handed them back to their superiors, who imprisoned most of them, and four were burned at Marseille in 1318. 'Ginhac': the printed 'ginhaco dyocesis bitterrensis' is kept; the identification of the place is uncertain. Guiraud's refusal to swear to name others is the point at which the inquisition turned a suspect into an obstinate heretic.

units.titel: The sentence: Olivi, Babylon, and the secular arm
units.orig: […] Cum tamen in dicta exposicione super apocalipsim inveniantur plures articuli continentes hereses & errores, qui judicati sunt heretici ex sentencia & judicio examinacione previa diligenti octo magistrorum in theologica facultate, qui auctoritate & mandato domini pape ad examinandum eandem fuerunt positi & provisi. Multa sunt alia que isti presumptuosi homines de cursu temporum & fine seculi sompniant, que de antichristi adventu quem jam instare asserunt flebili vanitate divulgant, que omnia quia partim heretica partim insana partim fabulosa esse dinoscuntur dampnanda pocius cum suis actoribus quam stilo persequenda censenda sunt, quia nec racione vigent nec auctoritate constant nec aliqua veri similitudine fulciuntur. In hujusmodi doctrinis variis & peregrinis sepe nominati homines simplicium corda blandis fictisque sermonibus & simulate humilitatis pretextu & habitu attrahere moliuntur. Igitur quia dignum est ut adversus illos ecclesiastica censura consurgat qui potestatem apostolicam prophanis vocum novitatibus & impiis assercionibus lacerando conculcant, & quandam ecclesiam esse confingunt quam consistere dicunt in congregacione sui & suorum sibi similium dampnatorum, Romanam vero ecclesiam dicunt esse illam babilonem meretricem magnam quam Johannes in apocalipsi detestatur, applicantes ad hoc exposicionem reprobam & hereticam prefati Petri Johannis super apocalipsim quem sanctum patrem & magnum doctorem nominant. In hiis se ipsos scismatice manifeste dividunt à sancte Romane ecclesie unitate. Idcirco nos prefati inquisitor ac vicarius & conmissarius, quia prenominati Petrus hospitalis & Petrus guiraudi in profundum malorum descendentes in predictorum errorum ac dogmatis pravitate persistunt animis induratis, eosdem errores procaciter & pertinaciter defendentes eisdemque inherentes mori in ipsis & pro ipsis pocius eligunt quam converti, […] dicimus & per diffinitivam sentenciam declaramus, predictos Petrum hospitalis ac Petrum Guiraudi esse assertores pestilentes perversorum dogmatum ac rebelles auctoritati & potestati apostolice sedis & Romani pontificis, nec non ipsos esse hereticos manifestos, dictumque Petrum hospitalis nichilominus esse relapsum in heresim à se prius in judicio abjuratam, eumdemque ac Petrum guiraudi predictum velut hereticos obstinatos relinquimus brachio & judicio curie secularis affectuose rogantes prout suadent canonice sancciones venerabilem & discretum virum dominum Johannem Marchi judicem majorem tenentemque locum domini senescalli Tholose aliosque curiales & officiales curie ut circa ipsos citra mortem & membrorum mutilacionem suum judicium & sentenciam moderentur. Lata fuit hec sentencia fueruntque facte gracie & injuncte penitencie & late diffinitive sentencie & acta omnia alia que in presenti sermone superius continentur. Anno die & loco & presentibus testibus supra scriptis in principio hujus presentis sermonis.
units.en: […] Whereas in that exposition of the Apocalypse many articles are found containing heresies and errors, which have been judged heretical by the sentence and judgement, after diligent examination, of eight masters of the faculty of theology, who were appointed and assigned to examine it by the authority and command of the lord pope. There are many other things that these presumptuous men dream about the course of the times and the end of the world, which they spread with lamentable vanity about the coming of Antichrist, who they say is already at hand; all of which, since they are known to be partly heretical, partly insane and partly fabulous, are to be judged fit to be condemned together with their authors rather than to be pursued with the pen, since they have no force of reason, no standing of authority and no support of likelihood. With such varied and outlandish doctrines the men often named try to draw the hearts of simple people by smooth and feigned words and under the pretext and habit of feigned humility. Therefore, since it is fitting that the censure of the Church should rise against those who trample on the apostolic power, tearing it with profane novelties of words and impious assertions, and who invent a certain church which they say consists in the congregation of themselves and of the condemned who are like them, and say that the Roman Church is that Babylon the great whore which John abhors in the Apocalypse, applying to this the reprobate and heretical exposition of the said Peter John on the Apocalypse, whom they call a holy father and a great doctor; in which they plainly divide themselves schismatically from the unity of the holy Roman Church: therefore we, the said inquisitor, vicar and commissary, since the said Pierre Hospitalis and Pierre Guiraud, descending into the depth of evils, persist with hardened hearts in the depravity of these errors and this doctrine, defending the same errors boldly and pertinaciously, and cleaving to them choose rather to die in them and for them than to be converted, […] say, and by definitive sentence declare, that the said Pierre Hospitalis and Pierre Guiraud are pestilent assertors of perverse doctrines and rebels against the authority and power of the apostolic see and of the Roman pontiff, and are manifest heretics; and that the said Pierre Hospitalis has moreover relapsed into the heresy he formerly abjured in court; and we leave him and the said Pierre Guiraud, as obstinate heretics, to the arm and judgement of the secular court, affectionately asking, as the canonical sanctions advise, the venerable and discreet man lord Jean Marchi, chief judge and lieutenant of the lord seneschal of Toulouse, and the other officers and officials of the court, to moderate their judgement and sentence concerning them short of death and the mutilation of limbs. This sentence was pronounced, and the graces granted, the penances imposed, the definitive sentences pronounced and all the other acts that are contained above in the present sermon were done, in the year, on the day and at the place, and before the witnesses, written above at the beginning of this present sermon.
units.note: 12 September 1322. 'They choose rather to die in them and for them than to be converted': the sentence itself records that the two knew what the relaxation meant. The eight masters' examination of Olivi's commentary preceded John XXII's condemnation of it (1326). With this sermon ends the book's last group of Beguin sentences. Fourteen months later, on 12 November 1323, the pope declared heretical the very assertion Pierre Hospitalis held, that Christ and the apostles had nothing, of their own or in common (Decr. Nonnullos [1]); the Beguins had been burned for the Franciscan doctrine before the pope condemned it, and for disobedience to a decretal the order itself obeyed.
